source_span: Jay Barry thinks if Core MoM prints in the +0.1% to +0.2% range then the FED WILL HOLD, assuming NFP prints ~50k and unemployment rate is steady... Goldilocks is like in the 30k – 70k range.
source_chain: Waller's dovish, data-dependent hold stance needs confirming data, therefore NFP landing near ~50k (inside JPM's 30k-70k 'Goldilocks' band) with unemployment steady keeps the hold condition alive only if core CPI also prints +0.1%-0.2% on Sep 11, therefore CPI (not NFP) is the actual decisive test, invalidated if NFP deviates far from ~50k or CPI runs hot.
pulse_chain: NFP printed 162k, roughly 3x the Street's 55k and far outside JPM's own 30k-70k Goldilocks band, therefore the NFP leg of JPM's explicit hold condition (~50k) is already broken; combined with ISM services prices-paid at a four-year high (a series that leads CPI by months), the disinflation read behind Waller's dovish repricing is undercut, therefore Sep 11 core CPI at JPM's same 0.1%-0.2% threshold is the level that now decides whether the hold survives.
why: The pulse carries JPM's own quantified hold condition (core CPI 0.1%-0.2% plus NFP ~50k) and its Sep 11 CPI invalidation through intact, correctly identifying that the NFP leg of that exact condition just broke, attributed to the same bank and in the same direction as the source.
